title: Nvidia's board prepares to replace CEO Jensen Huang, and the stock falls about 8% after hours
tldr: Nvidia's board met to prepare for removing co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after two reported affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy; the shares fell about 8% in after-hours trading.
byline: TechCrunch, Fortune, The Globe and Mail

title: UK economy grows 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest pace in more than two years
tldr: UK GDP rose 0.7% from July to September, led by services such as computer programming tied to cloud and AI spending, despite higher energy prices from the Iran war.

title: EU court adviser says Google's annulled 1.49 billion euro AdSense fine was wrongly scrapped
tldr: Advocate General Juliane Kokott told the EU's top court that a lower court erred in 2024 when it annulled Google's AdSense fine, and proposed sending the case back for a new ruling.

title: Canadian Tire beats profit estimates as higher gas prices lift sales, and raises its dividend
tldr: Canadian Tire's third-quarter profit rose to $246.4 million, beating forecasts, as pricier gasoline boosted sales; comparable sales rose 4.4%, or 1.7% without its gas business.
byline: The Globe and Mail, Canadian Tire Corporation (newswire)

title: The Main Monetary Policy Shock
tldr: Combining three kinds of Fed announcement surprises, the authors find monetary policy shocks explain about 18% of swings in consumer prices over four years, far more than prior work suggested.
byline: Christoph Boehm, Husang Kim, T. Niklas Kroner · University of Texas at Austin, Federal Reserve Board of Governors

title: US consumer prices rise 0.4% in October, more than forecast, keeping a December Fed hike in play
tldr: The US consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% analysts expected but slower than September's 0.6%, as energy price increases eased.

title: Bank of Canada notes show it hiked because energy costs were starting to spread, and it may go further
tldr: The Bank of Canada's summary of its October 28 deliberations shows officials raised the rate to 2.5% to stop high energy prices becoming broad inflation and did not rule out more hikes.

title: Boeing to cut about 5% of its commercial airplane workforce as it slows its production ramp-up
tldr: Boeing will cut roughly 5% of its commercial airplane staff through layoffs and attrition after slowing plans to raise jet output, with layoff notices starting in December.

title: Children's Place files for bankruptcy and puts its kidswear brands up for sale
tldr: Children's Place, owner of the Gymboree brand, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection and set a December 9 deadline for bids on its assets after falling sales and mounting losses.

title: Unconventional Monetary Policy and Deposit Retention
tldr: Years of zero interest rates and Fed bond buying filled US banks with rate-sensitive depositors, which made keeping deposits costlier and riskier once rates rose in 2015 and 2022.
byline: Philip Strahan, Tuo Yang · Boston College

title: Anthropic sets a $70 to $78 price range for an IPO that could raise up to $64.4 billion
tldr: Anthropic's filing shows an indicative range of $70 to $78 a share and up to $64.4 billion raised, the first public-market test of frontier AI valuations.

title: Fed's Waller backs a December hike even if October inflation cools, and floats a half-point move
tldr: Governor Waller said he would support a quarter-point hike in December regardless of October's CPI, and a half-point if core prices rose 0.3 percent or more.
byline: Federal Reserve, The Globe and Mail

title: California voters reject a one-time 5% tax on billionaires after a record-spending campaign
tldr: Californians defeated Proposition 40, a one-time 5% wealth tax on residents worth over $1 billion, after opponents spent nearly $425 million.

title: Financial Advisors and Retirees' Risk-taking
tldr: Retirees with financial advisors hold about two-thirds of their portfolios in stocks, 30 to 40 percentage points more than comparable retirees without one.
byline: Allison T. Cole, Maarten Meeuwis, Alessandro Previtero et al.

title: Canada launches its instant payments system, the last G7 country to do so
tldr: Payments Canada began the first phase of its Real-Time Rail on Monday, nearly seven years after the original 2019 target, with eight institutions but none of the big banks.

title: Strathcona agrees to buy Greenfire in a deal worth up to C$2.9 billion
tldr: Strathcona Resources will acquire Greenfire Resources for shares or C$11.00 in cash per share, valuing the deal at about C$2.7 to 2.9 billion including debt, with the same fund controlling both.
byline: Greenfire Resources (company release), The Globe and Mail

title: AI as Shared Business Infrastructure: Firm Growth and the Distribution of Gains
tldr: On a Chinese e-commerce platform, small firms that adopted built-in generative AI saw monthly sales rise 51.6%, with the biggest proportional gains for the smallest firms.
byline: Panle Jia Barwick, Lu Fang, Jinhan Liu et al.

title: US hiring surprises at 165,000 jobs while Canada's labour market weakens, with unemployment at 4.1% and 6.7%
tldr: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October versus about 65,000 expected, while Canada lost 4,700 jobs and its unemployment rate rose to 6.7%, widening the gap between the two labour markets.
byline: Statistics Canada, Associated Press via The Globe and Mail, Reuters via The Globe and Mail

title: Canada's 2026 budget moves bank anti-money-laundering supervision to OSFI and proposes tax simplifications
tldr: Ottawa's budget shifts supervision of banks' anti-money-laundering work from FinTRAC to OSFI, offers modest corporate tax simplification, and a follow-on reform loosens temporary foreign worker limits.
byline: Budget 2026, Government of Canada, The Globe and Mail, The Globe and Mail

title: The Effects of Monetary Policy on Macroeconomic Expectations: High-Frequency Evidence from Prediction Markets
tldr: Using minute-by-minute prices of Kalshi prediction-market contracts, the authors find macro expectations respond to Fed announcements as standard theory predicts, with little or no "Fed information effect".
byline: Eric T. Swanson, Wang Renxuan, Yanbin Wu

title: Wall Street's AI-driven rout deepens after the midterms and spreads across Asia
tldr: US stocks fell sharply on Thursday as investors feared Democratic control of Congress could slow the AI buildout, and the losses spread to Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Friday.
byline: The Guardian (live, Nov 6), The Guardian (Nov 4), The Globe and Mail (Reuters)

title: Tesla says it will stop making the Cybertruck next year to make room for the Cybercab
tldr: Elon Musk said Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production in 2027, using the factory space for its two-seat Cybercab robotaxi after years of weak sales.

title: Aggregate-Surplus Maximizing Monetary Policy
tldr: A new NBER paper finds that when households differ in labor-market frictions, a central bank maximizing everyone's joint surplus should weight output stabilization about 37 percent more than inflation, compared with the standard model.
byline: David Baqaee, Ariel Burstein, Joao Guerreiro

title: Bank of England raises its rate to 4%, the first increase in more than three years
tldr: The Bank of England voted 8-1 to lift Bank Rate to 4% from 3.75%, saying energy-driven inflation pressure in the pipeline is now strong enough to justify tighter policy.

title: ECB wage tracker points to slightly firmer negotiated pay growth into 2027
tldr: The ECB's wage tracker shows negotiated wage growth of 2.7% in late 2026 and 2.8% in early 2027, a little higher than the 2.3% headline figure for 2026 as a whole.

title: US trade deficit narrows slightly to $105.0 billion in September as exports and imports both rise
tldr: The US goods and services trade deficit eased by $0.7 billion to $105.0 billion in September, though the three-month average deficit widened to $101.2 billion.

title: Canada's trade surplus widens to a four-year high as gold and energy offset tariff-hit exports
tldr: Canada's September merchandise trade surplus widened to about C$5.4 billion, the highest since May 2022, but gold and oil hid a 5.6% drop in other exports hit by US tariffs.
byline: Statistics Canada, The Globe and Mail

title: Demand-Driven Inflation
tldr: Giannone and Primiceri argue that unexpectedly strong demand, not supply shocks alone, drove the post-pandemic inflation surge in both the United States and the euro area.
byline: Domenico Giannone, Giorgio Primiceri · Johns Hopkins University; Northwestern University

title: US tech stocks rebound as an AI-spending selloff ends on election day
tldr: US tech shares recovered on Tuesday after a week-long AI selloff, with oil easing from $117 to $103 a barrel, while investors largely looked past the midterm elections.

title: Canva to cut or relocate 1,271 jobs as growth slows
tldr: Design-software firm Canva is restructuring 22% of its workforce, 1,271 people, after growth slowed for the first time in a decade and AI costs rose.

title: Foodtastic bids $1 billion for MTY Food Group as MTY replaces its CEO
tldr: Foodtastic took a $43-a-share cash offer for MTY directly to shareholders after MTY's board refused talks, on the same day MTY abruptly replaced its CEO.

title: Shopify shares drop 12.8% at the open despite 31.5% revenue growth
tldr: Shopify's third-quarter revenue of US$3.742 billion grew 31.5% but missed analyst expectations by a hair, and the stock fell as expectations were high.

title: US factory orders jump 1.8% in September on aircraft and AI build-out
tldr: New orders for US factory goods rose 1.8% in September, beating the 1.2% forecast, helped by aircraft bookings and AI infrastructure, though economists warn of headwinds next year.
